Solve an MPS file and write a solution file

Source: R/solve_engines.R
solve_mps.Rd

Reads an MPS file written by write_mps(), solves it and writes a solution file that read_mps_solution() decodes against the index tables.

Usage

solve_mps(
  file,
  sol_file = NULL,
  control = list(),
  require_optimal = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  solver = c("highs", "julia_highs", "cuopt"),
  where = c("local", "wsl")
)

Arguments

file

Path to the MPS file. HiGHS in this process reads it uncompressed; cuOpt reads .gz as well.

sol_file

Path for the solution file; default file with a .sol extension, in the directory of file.

control

Solver options; see Details.

require_optimal

Logical; error unless the run ends optimal.

verbose

Logical; report progress.

solver

"highs", "julia_highs" or "cuopt".

where

"local" or "wsl".

Value

A list with status_message, objective, sol_file and run_time (seconds).

Details

Solvers and places:

  • "highs", "local": HiGHS in this R process (the highs package).

  • "julia_highs", "local": HiGHS through Julia (HiGHS.jl), whose build carries the HiPO interior point method. Julia is found by get_multimod_julia().

  • "cuopt", "local": NVIDIA cuOpt's cuopt_cli on this machine (Linux).

  • "cuopt", "wsl": cuopt_cli inside WSL on a local GPU (Windows); the solution is written inside WSL and copied out in one piece.

control holds the solver's options. HiGHS (both places): named HiGHS options, e.g. list(solver = "ipm"). cuOpt: method (default 1, PDLP), time_limit (seconds; cuopt_cli's own default is short), presolve, options (further cuopt_cli flags as one string or a character vector); for "wsl" also wsl_user and cuopt_cli (path inside WSL), else the environment variables MULTIMOD_WSL_USER and MULTIMOD_CUOPT_CLI, else WSL's default user and cuopt_cli on its PATH.

A cuOpt run (any place) can go through cuOpt's Python interface instead of cuopt_cli (control$api = "python"). It writes the solution file whatever the status: at a time limit the current iterate is kept (status TimeLimit), where cuopt_cli writes no values. control$save_warm_start = TRUE also returns PDLP's warm-start data as warm_start.pkl beside sol_file; control$warm_start (a path to such a file) continues from it. Both run PDLP in its Stable2 mode, the one cuOpt warm-starts, and without cuOpt's presolve (unless control$presolve is set): the warm-start data has the size of the problem PDLP solved. Locally and in WSL the Python is control$cuopt_python, else the environment variable MULTIMOD_CUOPT_PYTHON, else python3 beside cuopt_cli.

Scripts and parameter files a solver needs go to temporary files and are removed afterwards; the cuOpt log goes to control$log_file, else to a temporary file. Only the solution (and, when asked, the warm-start data) is written beside sol_file.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)) {
  dir <- tempfile("mps-")
  dir.create(dir)
  mps <- file.path(dir, "toy.mps")
  write_mps(example_models$toy, mps, format = "csv")
  s <- solve_mps(mps)
  s$objective
  sol <- read_mps_solution(s$sol_file, index_dir = dir, format = "csv")
  head(sol$primal)
}
